consumer_contexts: room-scale and seated games shipped on several headset platforms that must offer teleport, snap or smooth turn, and continuous movement as a person's choice with a comfort policy the platform review can inspect
training, industrial, and accessibility XR applications that move a person between authored anchors, constrain movement by posture, and replay a session deterministically for review
common_kernel: a closed set of locomotion modes (teleport, snap turn, smooth turn, continuous move) as validated identities separate from the provider, rig, or input that implements them
a comfort policy as a closed set of typed options (vignette, turn mode, turn increment, movement speed, posture) with declared ranges and fail-closed rejection
locomotion intents (teleport to an anchor id, turn by an increment, move a vector for a tick) applied to an immutable state with stable failure codes
deterministic replay of an intent sequence to an equal state and fingerprint
configurable_variation: the admitted increment set, speed range, vignette intensity range, default posture, and which modes a product enables
adapter-side binding to XR Interaction Toolkit providers, input action references, forward source, gravity, and vignette parameters
consumer-owned anchors, rig prefab, scene layout, and platform comfort presets
excluded_project_specific: one product's comfort preset values, level layout, teleport anchor set, and rig prefab
one project's input bindings, boundary handling, fade art, and platform store comfort rating
rationale: Locomotion and comfort are a recurring cross-project need whose kernel (a closed mode set, a typed comfort policy, anchor-referenced teleport and increment-based turn intents, and deterministic state) is shared by the engine's own locomotion providers, three platform comfort guidelines, and two independent open-source implementations, while every product keeps its own anchors, presets, rig, input bindings, and comfort rating outside the shared Core.
non_claims: Admission does not claim motion sickness reduction, comfort, latency, frame timing, rig motion, input reading, tracking, boundary behaviour, or any named-device behaviour; those require a Device Lab receipt.

This draft becomes a decision only when a maintainer copies it into docs/foundry/admissions/ after a person confirms the sources, page paths, versions, and the maintenance state of each open-source implementation.
